test.title: The lead technician dialog lists only eligible technicians, no Unassigned
test.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard), {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) and {Technician-C} (for example Dana Ortiz) are active staff members at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Staff member {User-B} (for example Owen Office) is active at {Location-A} with the Office User role.
  • Technician {Technician-D} (for example Ivan Inactive) has a Technician role at {Location-A} and is deactivated.
  • Technician {Technician-E} (for example Lena Otherloc) is active with Time Clock on but works only at another location, {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310).
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Reassign List") has one Approved work order, {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17641), led by {Technician-A}.
  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for {Work-order-1}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
  • Developer note kept from the automation engineer (nothing for the tester to do): Dev-layer test — fe-unit + be-functional. Existing coverage: ReassignLeadTechnicianDialog.spec.ts:279,463; BE ListLeadTechnicianCandidatesTest.php:59,65
test.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Hover {Work-order-1}'s card in {Technician-A}'s column and click its More actions (…) button.
  4. Click Reassign lead technician.
  5. Read every row in the dialog, from the top.
  6. Click {Technician-B}'s row.
  7. If a "Clear … scheduled shifts?" question opens, click Keep shifts.
  8. Hover the card, now in {Technician-B}'s column, and click its More actions (…) button.
  9. Click Unassign.
  10. If a "Clear … scheduled shifts?" question opens, click Keep shifts.
  11. Hover the card, now in the Unassigned column, click its More actions (…) button and click Assign lead technician.
  12. Type the first letters of {Technician-C}'s name in the dialog's search box, then click Cancel.
  13. Click the card to open the work order and read Lead Technician.
  14. Press the browser Back button and click Tech View in the display switcher.
  15. Hover {Work-order-1}'s row in the Unassigned group, click its More actions (…) button and click Assign lead technician.
  16. Read every row in the dialog, from the top.
  17. Click {Technician-A}'s row.
  18. If a "Clear … scheduled shifts?" question opens, click Keep shifts.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: the dialog opens with the title "Reassign lead technician".
  • Step 5: the dialog has a Search technicians box, then one list with no grouping of the eligible technicians of {Location-A}, {Technician-A}, {Technician-B} and {Technician-C}, each with an avatar and an "N open" count. There is no Unassigned row. {User-B}, {Technician-D} and {Technician-E} are not listed. The only button is Cancel.
  • Step 6: the dialog closes at once, with no other click, and the card moves to {Technician-B}'s column. The message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with an Undo button.
  • Step 9: the card moves to the Unassigned column and the message "{Work-order-1} moved to Unassigned" shows, with an Undo button.
  • Step 11: the menu offers "Assign lead technician" (not "Reassign lead technician"), and the dialog opens with the title "Assign lead technician".
  • Step 12: the dialog closes and nothing changes: the card stays in the Unassigned column.
  • Step 13: the work order page shows no lead technician.
  • Step 16: the Tech View dialog, titled "Assign lead technician", shows the same technicians as at step 5, with no Unassigned row.
  • Step 17: the dialog closes at once and the row moves to {Technician-A}'s group. The message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-A}" shows, with an Undo button.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S3-R14, S4-R4, S4-R12, S4-R13, S4-R14 and S4-R5, read 19 Oct 2026. Eligibility from PRD section 5 Terminology (Technician) and S2-R7. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 19, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 19) that the dialog is final as drawn (search, avatars, N open per technician, no grouping) with Unassigned as its first row, and PRD version 54 said so. PRD version 66 (19 Oct 2026, after SV-11522 and SV-11524) took Unassigned out of the dialog, made a click on a technician assign at once, and named the menu item and the dialog "Assign lead technician" or "Reassign lead technician"; removing the lead is the menu's Unassign action. This case follows PRD version 68, which is later.

Known problem (SV-11522 and SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the More actions menu on a work order with no lead says "Reassign lead technician"; the lead technician dialog lists "Unassigned" at the top, and choosing a technician needs a click on a "Reassign" button; the message after a lead change reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R14: “Include the lead technician action in the card’s more-actions menu: “Assign lead technician” on a work order with no lead technician, “Reassign lead technician” on one that has a lead technician.”
  • S4-R4: “The card or row more-actions menu opens the lead technician dialog, titled “Assign lead technician” or “Reassign lead technician” to match the menu item it was opened from (S3-R14).”
  • S4-R12: “The dialog offers eligible active technicians in the current location and nothing else. Unassigned is not offered there: Unassigned is the place for work orders without a lead, not a technician, and removing the lead is the menu’s Unassign action (S11-R9) or a drag to Unassigned. It follows the design: a Search technicians box, each technician with their avatar and N open count, no grouping.”
  • S4-R13: “Clicking a technician in the dialog assigns them at once; there is no confirm button, and the dialog’s only button is Cancel. When the shift-clearing prompt applies (S4-R28) it shows first, and the change is made from the prompt. Clicking the work order’s current lead closes the dialog with no change (S4-N4).”
  • S4-R14: “Canceling the dialog leaves the lead unchanged.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”

test.title: Lead change messages name the work order and close on their own
test.custom_preconds:
Dev-layer test — fe-unit. Existing coverage: useReassignLeadTechnician.spec.ts:450,472 (auto-close check lives in E2E C96959)

Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 10 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • Two eligible technicians at this location: [Tech-A] (e.g. "Esther Howard") and [Tech-B] "Ralph Edwards". A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Messages" (used by this case only) with one Approved work order [WO-1] led by [Tech-A].
  • Ralph Edwards is named in the expected results and stays as written; the other names and the number are examples.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard), [Tech-B] = "Ralph Edwards" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Messages" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Messages": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-702): Lead Technician = [Tech-A].
  6. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Messages" shows [WO-1] with Lead Technician [Tech-A]. If not, fix it on the work order page before starting; then clear the search.

test.title: The lead of an Invoiced or Paid work order cannot be changed in any way
test.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Invoiced Paid Locked") is used by this case only and has six work orders whose Lead Technician was set while they were still open (for example S10043-17801 to S10043-17806): {Work-order-1} Approved, led by {Technician-A}; {Work-order-2} Invoiced, led by {Technician-A}; {Work-order-3} Paid, led by {Technician-A}; {Work-order-4} Invoiced, with no lead technician; {Work-order-5} Declined, led by {Technician-A}; {Work-order-6} Complete, led by {Technician-A}.
  • {Technician-B} is not the technician on any line of these work orders.
  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
test.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
  4. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card into the Unassigned column.
  5. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card within {Technician-A}'s column to above {Work-order-1}.
  6. Drag {Work-order-3}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column, then into the Unassigned column, then within {Technician-A}'s column to above {Work-order-1}.
  7. Drag {Work-order-4}'s card into {Technician-A}'s column, then drag it to a new place within the Unassigned column.
  8. Drag {Work-order-5}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column (click Keep shifts if asked).
  9. Drag {Work-order-6}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column (click Keep shifts if asked).
  10. Open {Work-order-2} and try to change Lead Technician on the work order page.
  11. Go back, click Tech View in the display switcher and do steps 3 to 7 again with the rows, then drag {Work-order-5} and {Work-order-6} from {Technician-B}'s group back into {Technician-A}'s group.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 3, 4 and 6: {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3} cannot be moved to {Technician-B} or to Unassigned: the card goes back to {Technician-A}'s column and the lead stays {Technician-A}. While {Work-order-2}'s card is over {Technician-B}'s column, the note "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" shows at the top of that column; for {Work-order-3} it reads "Paid · can’t be reassigned".
  • Steps 5 and 6: {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3} can be moved within {Technician-A}'s column and keep their new place.
  • Step 7: {Work-order-4} cannot be moved out of Unassigned, but it can be reordered inside it.
  • Steps 8 and 9: {Work-order-5} (Declined) and {Work-order-6} (Complete) move to {Technician-B} normally, with the messages "{Work-order-5} assigned to {Technician-B}" and "{Work-order-6} assigned to {Technician-B}", each with an "Undo" button.
  • Step 10: on the work order page the Lead Technician of {Work-order-2} cannot be changed either.
  • Step 11: Tech View follows the same rules for every move (the note shows at the top of {Technician-B}'s group). A change sent outside the screens is also refused by the server; this part cannot be checked by hand, so write "server refusal not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see. Imported work orders are checked in their own case.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R10, S4-N2, S4-N6, S4-R5 and Key decision: lead locked once Invoiced or Paid, read 19 Oct 2026. In version 48 (12 Oct 2026) S4-N2 dropped Imported from the locked statuses (Imported work orders now open in List only); the Invoiced and Paid rules this case checks are unchanged, so the expected results are unchanged. Review Decisions DR-37 (Declined and Complete move freely). PO answer to engineering, Sasha Grosman 24 Sep 2026 (Invoiced/Paid reorder within their technician or within Unassigned). In versions 66 to 68 (19 Oct 2026) the Invoiced or Paid rule was extended to Unassign and Undo, S4-N6 gave the drag note the design's words, and the message after a move became "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}", with Undo; the results of steps 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 11 follow.   3. Record them as [Tech-A] = "Esther Howard" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it), [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards).

On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). test.title: Moving to another technician shows the message, reordering shows none
test.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 10 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders). This user is the dispatcher.
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  • Technicians (examples, the expected results call them by first name or full name): "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo". A staff member counts as a technician when, in Settings > Staff > the staff member's edit icon > Edit Staff Member, they are Active, Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customers (used by this case only, each with one contact and one asset): "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message Bravo Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message Charlie Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message Delta Co". The steps and expected results call them by the end of the name ("Alpha Co", "Bravo Co", "Charlie Co", "Delta Co").

Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo" exist and count as technicians at this location (edit icon > Edit Staff Member).   2. Create this case's customers: "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message Bravo Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message Charlie Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message Delta Co". For each: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name > Save; on the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact); then the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  3. Create each work order listed in the Preconditions: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. Move it to the status named: a new work order starts as Estimate (it opens with the New Line form: pick a ready-made line and Save & Close); for Approved turn on Line Approved on its line; for In Progress click Start on the line's Labor row (stop the clock afterwards with Stop > Clock Out); for Review click the line's Complete button, type a Tech Story (fill any missing detail it asks for, e.g. Mileage) and click Complete Line (the List shows "Ready For Review"); for Complete then click Mark Reviewed, enter the VIN if asked and click Confirm Review; for Declined save the line with Line Approved off and click Decline on it (it must be the work order's only line); for Invoiced complete and review it first, then Finance tab > Create Invoice; for Paid, after invoicing, Finance tab > New Payment for the full amount > Make Payment. Set the lead technician before invoicing. Once the work order is Approved, pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page (leave it as Unassigned for an unassigned one). (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Write down each work order number as you create it (e.g. S1-801); the steps call each work order by the end of its customer name (e.g. "Alpha Co").
  4. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > List > type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message" in Search — exactly 4 work orders show, all Approved: 3 led by Ana, Delta Co led by Ben. If anything differs, correct that work order (status or Lead Technician) before starting.
test.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Move Message" in Search so only this case's work orders show.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher (tooltip "Board View").
  4. Write down the header counts (Ana 3, Ben 1).
  5. Drag the Alpha Co card from Ana's column into Ben's column and release. Do not reload.
  6. Read the message that appears and both header counts, then wait about 10 seconds without clicking or pointing at the message.
  7. Drag the Alpha Co card above the Delta Co card inside Ben's column and release.
  8. Read the screen for any message, read both header counts, then open Alpha Co and read Lead Technician.

  • Step 6: a message naming the work order and Ben appears, with an Undo button (e.g. "S1-801 assigned to ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo", with Alpha Co's own number), and the counts change at once to Ana 2, Ben 2 (3 − 1 = 2 and 1 + 1 = 2), with no page reload. The message closes by itself within the 10 seconds (after about 5 seconds).
  • Step 8: Alpha Co moves above Delta Co. No message appears, the counts stay Ana 2, Ben 2, and Alpha Co still has Lead Technician Ben Bravo.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R5: “Successful between-technician moves use Story 4’s feedback and count updates.”
  • S9-R15: “Reordering within one technician changes position without changing assignments or showing a reassignment toast.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • S4-R7: “Counts in column/group headers update immediately after a successful change.”
  • S4-R16: “The lead-change toast closes on its own after 5 seconds (5,000 ms) while it carries the Undo button, and after 2.6 seconds (2,600 ms) without one, as in the design; it stays open while the pointer is over it, and closes when Undo is clicked. Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Invoiced Lock") is used by this case only and has six work orders (for example S10043-17811 to S10043-17816): {Work-order-1} Approved, {Work-order-2} Invoiced, {Work-order-3} Paid, {Work-order-4} Declined and {Work-order-5} Complete, all led by {Technician-A}, and {Work-order-6} Invoiced with no lead technician.
  • {Technician-B} is not the technician on any line of these work orders.
  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
test.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Look at the {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3} cards and hover the lock or any marker on them.
  5. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card above {Work-order-1}'s card inside {Technician-A}'s column and release it.
  6. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column and release it.
  7. Drag {Work-order-3}'s card into the Unassigned column and release it.
  8. Drag {Work-order-6}'s card from Unassigned into {Technician-A}'s column and release it.
  9. Drag {Work-order-4}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column and release it, then drag {Work-order-5}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column and release it.
  10. Click Tech View in the display switcher.
  11. Drag {Work-order-3}'s row into {Technician-B}'s group and release it.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3} each show a lock icon, which marks that they can only be reordered within {Technician-A}'s work, not moved to another technician. Hovering the lock shows "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" on {Work-order-2} and "Paid · can’t be reassigned" on {Work-order-3}.
  • Step 5: {Work-order-2} moves above {Work-order-1}. Reordering within the same technician is allowed.
  • Steps 6 and 7: {Work-order-2} cannot be dropped on {Technician-B} and {Work-order-3} cannot be dropped on Unassigned. While {Work-order-2} is over {Technician-B}'s column, the note "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" shows at the top of that column. Both stay in {Technician-A}'s column, no lead-change message appears and {Technician-A}'s count is unchanged.
  • Step 8: {Work-order-6} cannot be moved out of Unassigned. It stays there.
  • Step 9: {Work-order-4} (Declined) and {Work-order-5} (Complete) move to {Technician-B}'s column, with the messages "{Work-order-4} assigned to {Technician-B}" and "{Work-order-5} assigned to {Technician-B}", each with an "Undo" button.
  • Step 11: the same rule holds in Tech View. While {Work-order-3}'s row is over {Technician-B}'s group, the note "Paid · can’t be reassigned" shows at the top of that group, and {Work-order-3} stays in {Technician-A}'s group.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S9-N1, S4-N2, S4-N7, S4-N6 and S4-R5, read 19 Oct 2026. In version 48 (12 Oct 2026) S4-N2 dropped Imported from the locked statuses (Imported work orders now open in List only); the Invoiced and Paid rules this case checks are unchanged, so the expected results are unchanged. In version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling on the design-difference sheet) S4-N6 gave the lock icon and the drag note the design's words, and S4-R5 made the message after a move "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}", with Undo; the results of steps 4, 6, 9 and 11 follow. Review Decisions page 853901313, DR-37 (25 Sep 2026). Tech plan (revised 24 Sep 2026) section 3.23. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message after a lead change reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-N1: “Apply S4-N1 and S4-N2’s permission and status restrictions to every work order drag.”
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Invoiced or Paid status. An Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Declined and Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today.”
  • S4-N7: “Visually indicate that an Invoiced or Paid work order can only be reordered within its current technician, not moved to another one.”
  • S4-N6: “On an Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • Tech plan 3.23 lead lock vs reorder: “In a locked status a work order can be dragged within its current technician (or within Unassigned if it has no lead); it cannot be dropped on another technician, and cannot move between a technician and Unassigned.”

test.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser with a tracker blocker · about 15 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders). This user is the dispatcher.
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  • Technicians (examples, the expected results call them by first name or full name): "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo". A staff member counts as a technician when, in Settings > Staff > the staff member's edit icon > Edit Staff Member, they are Active, Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customers (used by this case only, each with one contact and one asset): "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Blocked Analytics Alpha Co". The steps and expected results call them by the end of the name ("Alpha Co").
  • Work order Alpha Co: Approved, lead Ana; Ben is not the technician on its line.
  • Board View starting values: VIN/Serial off in Fields to display, Density not Compact.
  • None of these technicians has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders (check the Schedule page). If a window titled "Clear … scheduled shifts?" still appears during a move, click "Keep shifts".
  • Analytics blocked in your browser: a common tracker blocker extension (e.g. uBlock Origin) turned on for the QA site, or your browser's setting that blocks trackers.

Setup

  1. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo" exist and count as technicians at this location (edit icon > Edit Staff Member). To add one: New Staff Member with those settings (at least one Department is required) (e.g. first name "ZZAUTOTEST Ana", last name "Alpha") > Save & Close.
  2. Create this case's customers: "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Blocked Analytics Alpha Co". For each: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name > Save; on the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact); then the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  3. Create each work order listed in the Preconditions: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. Move it to the status named: a new work order starts as Estimate (it opens with the New Line form: pick a ready-made line and Save & Close); for Approved turn on Line Approved on its line; for In Progress click Start on the line's Labor row (stop the clock afterwards with Stop > Clock Out); for Review click the line's Complete button, type a Tech Story (fill any missing detail it asks for, e.g. Mileage) and click Complete Line (the List shows "Ready For Review"); for Complete then click Mark Reviewed, enter the VIN if asked and click Confirm Review; for Declined save the line with Line Approved off and click Decline on it (it must be the work order's only line); for Invoiced complete and review it first, then Finance tab > Create Invoice; for Paid, after invoicing, Finance tab > New Payment for the full amount > Make Payment. Set the lead technician before invoicing. Once the work order is Approved, pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page (leave it as Unassigned for an unassigned one). (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Write down each work order number as you create it (e.g. S1-801); the steps call each work order by the end of its customer name (e.g. "Alpha Co").
  4. Block analytics in your browser: install a common tracker blocker extension (e.g. uBlock Origin) and turn it on for the QA site, or use your browser's setting that blocks trackers.
  5. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > List > type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Blocked Analytics" in Search — exactly 1 work order shows: Alpha Co, Approved, lead Ana. In Board View, VIN/Serial is off and Density is not Compact (change them back if not). The blocker shows it is on for the QA site. If anything differs, correct that work order (status or Lead Technician) before starting.
test.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, search "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Blocked Analytics" and click Board View.

  • Step 4: after the refresh, Board View, VIN/Serial, Compact and Ben as lead are all still there. Analytics being blocked made no difference.

It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. test.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

test.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Drag {Work-order-1}'s card from Unassigned into {Technician-A}'s column and release it.
  3. Look at the message that appears.
  4. Wait ten seconds without moving the mouse over the message.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: a white message with a check icon reads “{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-A}” and has an “Undo” button. It is the design’s message for a lead change, not the app’s standard success message.
  • Step 4: the message closes by itself, about 5 seconds after it appeared.

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message after a lead change reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

  • Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign the lead technician). PRD “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), section 9 User Feedback Summary, S4-R5 and S4-R16, read 19 Oct 2026.
  • The product owner’s ruling on SV-11396 (16 Oct 2026), that this message uses the app’s standard success message, was reversed for these messages in PRD version 66 (19 Oct 2026; change log quoted below): the lead-change message is the design’s message, with Undo. Version 68 set its words and its closing time as in the design.
  • Updated 19 Oct 2026 to PRD version 68 (was: the app’s standard success message with the old wording, fading on its own, per the SV-11396 ruling).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • Section 9 User Feedback Summary, row (Trigger | Message | Behavior): “Lead technician changed by drag or the lead technician dialog (S4-R5) | “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”, or “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already on a line, with Undo | The design’s toast; closes after 5 seconds with Undo (2.6 seconds without), held while hovered (S4-R16); Undo restores the change (S4-R32)”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • S4-R16: “The lead-change toast closes on its own after 5 seconds (5,000 ms) while it carries the Undo button, and after 2.6 seconds (2,600 ms) without one, as in the design; it stays open while the pointer is over it, and closes when Undo is clicked. The “Assignment undone” toast (S4-R32) closes after 2.6 seconds. Other success toasts dismiss automatically, as today.”
  • PRD change log, 19 Oct 2026: “S4-R5, S4-R16, new S4-R32: the lead-change toast is the design’s toast, “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}” / “{work order number} unassigned”, with Undo; 8 seconds, held while hovered; Undo restores the lead, the order position and any cleared shifts (was: standard toast “Lead technician updated” / “Lead technician removed”, no Undo; reverses the SV-11396 call for these two toasts). v66.”
